title: docs: trim the computer bash tool description
author: voodoohop
pr_body_excerpt:
- Cuts the `bash` tool description from ~300 to ~200 tokens by dropping what the model can infer (heredoc alternatives, `sed -i`, `curl -o` syntax, the git subcommand list, "use head/tail for long output"); every inference-critical fact stays: persistence, `/tmp` reset, cwd default, no Node/Python, the stdin convention, `assets publish`, the 64 KB cap
- Shortens the server instructions and the two parameter descriptions that repeated it
- Fixes the docs page: `/tmp` is emptied after every call, and `assets publish` prints an unlisted URL that expires after 30 days, not a permanent public one

gist.headline: Less Bash, Same Roots
gist.blurb: The computer MCP's bash manual shed the parts a capable model already knows, while keeping the facts that prevent tiny terminal disasters. The /tmp garden now also has an accurately labeled 30-day exit sign.
gist.summary: Trimmed the computer MCP bash tool description from about 300 to 200 tokens while retaining persistence, per-call /tmp resets, default cwd, stdin conventions, no Node/Python, assets publish, and the 64 KB output cap; the MCP docs now clarify that assets publish URLs are unlisted and expire after 30 days.
gist.impact: Agents get a leaner bash prompt with the operational constraints they need, and developers now have accurate guidance that /tmp is cleared after every call and published asset links last 30 days.
gist.visual_concept: A cozy garden-shed terminal represents the computer MCP bash tool: Polli, wearing tiny librarian glasses, carefully prunes excess words from a scroll while preserving a few clearly labeled command-root notes. A small code-plant sits beside a /tmp bucket being emptied after each watering, and a 30-day sandglass beside an unlisted asset-link envelope visualizes the corrected documentation.
